growth_signal.value: Raised $250M in a Series D, bigger than its earlier $102M round.

entry.idea: People with paralysis cannot easily control computers, so Precision makes a thin brain implant that reads brain signals.
entry.lesson: In a hard science field, a gentler version of a scary technology can reach patients sooner.
entry.name: Precision Neuroscience

growth.basis: substitute: funding round bigger than the last ($250M vs $102M)
growth.reason: No user or revenue numbers, only a funding round larger than the last.

market.reason: Brain implants could help millions of people with paralysis and other conditions worldwide.

tech.reason: New hardware and science with regulatory clearance that is hard to copy for years.

entry.twist: The implant is very thin and goes on the brain surface with minimal surgery, and it has won FDA clearance.
entry.who_pays: Hospitals and health systems would pay for the implant; investors fund it until then.
entry.why_now: Better AI can decode brain signals, and investors are putting big money into Neuralink rivals.
